Upon hearing the counsel the Court made the following
 O R D E R
Heard the learned senior counsel for the petitioners as also learned senior counsel for the respondents and learned counsel for the State of Maharashtra.

Though we have heard the learned senior counsel elaborately on all aspects of the matter, we do not propose to advert to much of the details in as much as the instant proceedings has arisen out of a proceeding which has been initiated before the High Court and as a follow up of the said proceedings, presently, the petition in WP(c) No. 11473 of 2022 and Contempt Petition No. 682 of 2022 are pending before the High Court.

In that view, we are also conscious that any of the observations made herein on merits relating to the process of acquisition, it would affect the rights of the parties in the said pending proceedings and therefore we limit our consideration to the present short issue which has arisen herein.

In that regard, we note that the petitioner in SLP (C) Nos.23802-23805/2022 has assailed the orders dated 08.04.2022 and the consequential orders passed on the interim application in the disposed of Writ Petition No. 3119 of 2022.

The issue which arose therein is based on a writ petition which was filed by the respondents herein (New Millenium India Property Developers Pvt. Ltd.) seeking mandamus to the State of Maharashtra and the petitioner herein to take possession of the lands which were New Millenium India Developers Private ... vs Emerald Buildcon Pvt. 2 referred to therein since the acquisition proceedings for formation of the layout had commenced.

sentences.text: The acquisition was initiated under the Maharashtra Industrial Development Act, 1961.

In that regard, in the proceedings before the High Court, the State of Maharashtra, which is the acquiring authority had indicated that demand for payment was issued to the petitioner herein that is the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) which is the immediate beneficiary, to pay the amount.
The High Court having taken note of the same had directed that the deposit of the compensation be made by MIDC.

In the present proceedings the petitioner herein is contending that the award in respect of the entire extent of 63.232 hectares had not been passed by the SDO and as such the communication to deposit a sum of Rs. 86,94,40,000/- by the State Government and consequently the direction by the High Court against the MIDC at this juncture would not be justified.

We note that at the first instance when the petitioners had put forth the said contention and had indicated that they are ready to deposit the sum of Rs. 23.19 crores which is equivalent to the market value for 16.87 hectares of land for which award has been passed and there is no impediment
, this court through the order dated 15.12.2022 had directed them to deposit the same.
It is not in dispute that the said amount has been deposited by MIDC.
It is in that light, the issue raised herein presently relates to the remaining extent of the land regarding which rival contentions are being raised.

The learned senior counsel for the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 would point out that since the demand had been made by the State of Maharashtra through its communication dated 06.04.2022, the petitioner herein (MIDC) is obliged to deposit the entire amount in respect of the acquisition and cannot take a contrary stand.

On that aspect of the matter since we have already noted that the Writ Petition No.
11473 of 2022 is pending before the High Court, we refrain from expressing any opinion at this stage.

However, for the limited purpose of considering this petition, since we note that as on today,
the award passed is only in respect of 16.87 hectares and the amount equivalent to the same has been deposited by the petitioner (MIDC), in our opinion, until a decision is taken in the said pending writ petition with regard to the liability of MIDC also for the entire amount, the contempt proceedings against MIDC would not be justified.

To that extent we make it clear that in view of the fact that the petitioner namely, MIDC have deposited a portion of the amount which is equivalent to the extent of the land relating to which award is passed, we hold that the further action against petitioners would only depend on the ultimate decision to be taken in W.P.No. 11473 of 2022 but the contempt against them will not proceed.

Insofar as the contentions which have been urged in the said writ petition as also the contempt petition as against the State of Maharashtra, we express no opinion in these petitions and leave it open to be considered in the said proceedings based on the contentions to be put forth therein by the parties.
In SLP (C) 23596 of 2022, the New Millenium India Property Developers Pvt. Ltd., petitioners therein are assailing the order dated 01.12.2022.

In the said proceedings we note that the High Court in the Commercial Execution Petition having arrived at the conclusion that no portion of the amount undertaken to be paid has been paid, much less the sum of Rs.62.50 Crores has issued further directions with regard to the disclosure of the assets and an affidavit to be filed in that New Millenium India Developers Private ... vs Emerald Buildcon Pvt. Ltd. on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93691394/
3 regard.
The deposit to be made by the petitioner herein was dependent on the compensation which was to be paid by MIDC in the acquisition proceedings.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this juncture, we note that this Court through the order dated 09.01.2023 on taking note of the deposit made by the MIDC to the extent of 16.87 hectares had permitted that the said amount would be withdrawn by respondent No.7 i.e. the respondent in SLP (C) No.23596/2022 who is the applicant in Commercial Execution Application No. 4660 of 2022.

Hence, there is a change in circumstance, from that which existed as on the date when the High Court passed the order on 01.12.2022 inasmuch as the applicant therein has received a portion of the amount.
If that be the position, the High Court will have to take a fresh look into the matter and thereafter arrive at its conclusion.

To that extent, we clarify that the High Court before seeking compliance of the order dated 01.12.2022 by the defendants therein shall take note of the subsequent developments and pass fresh orders in accordance with law.

Considering that the issue between the parties has been lingering for quite some time, though the present writ petition pending before the High Court is of the year 2022, we request the High Court to consider and dispose of the proceedings as expeditiously as possible since it is brought to our notice that the pleadings are complete and the petitions are ready for hearing.
With the above observations and clarifications, the special leave petitions stand disposed of.
Pending application(s) shall also stand disposed of.
(RAJNI MUKHI) (DIPTI KHURANA)
